outcome: Still open on erdosproblems.com (#20, $1000) as of 13 October 2026; since 26 January 2024 there are restricted-class proofs (Balogh et al., Combinatorica, December 2025, for bounded VC-dimension; Ge et al., arXiv 2609.18995, July 2026, bounded VC-dimension; Mishra, arXiv 2606.02667, June 2026, shifted families), one unrefereed full-conjecture claim by Fukuyama whose arXiv version has been revised twice with the author stating each earlier version contained an error (current v3, 22 June 2026, unengaged), one full-conjecture claim retracted by its authors (Zenodo, January 2026), and several AI-assisted partial results on the Erdős forum that do not reach the general bound.
problem_asks: Unpacked from the statement alone. (1) For each fixed integer r > 2, i.e. every r = 3, 4, 5, ... taken one at a time; r = 3 is one part and is not the whole. (2) Whether there is a constant C = C(r), depending on r only and not on k, such that the number f(k,r) of sets needed is at most C^k, where f(k,r) is the least number such that every family of more than f(k,r) distinct k-element sets contains an r-sunflower (r distinct sets whose pairwise intersections are all one common kernel). (3) The bound must hold for all uniformities k, not for some k or for restricted families. The statement is an existence question ('can ... be bounded') and names no specific constant. Not asked by this bullet: the weak sunflower problem (Erdős #857), the Erdős–Szemerédi variant for subsets of [n], the Duke–Erdős forbidden sunflower problem, robust sunflowers, or families with bounded VC-dimension.

events.what_happened: Alweiss, Lovett, Wu and Zhang post 'Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma' (arXiv 1908.08483). Per the abstract they 'improve the bound to about (log w)^w' on families of w-sets with no r-sunflower, against the Erdős–Rado bound of about w^w, and note that the conjecture would give c^w. Published in Annals of Mathematics 194(3), 2021, pp. 795–815. Predates the window; recorded as the baseline the later work is measured against.
events.revisions: v2 16 Mar 2020; v3 31 Aug 2021; journal version Annals of Mathematics 194(3), 2021.
events.delivers: An upper bound for the sunflower threshold of order (log k)^k up to factors in r. Wikipedia quotes C = O(r^3 log k log log k) and Kalai's project page quotes (C r log k)^k. The base contains a log k factor, so the bound is exponential in the set size but not of the conjectured form C(r)^k. It neither confirms nor refutes the conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: a bound C(r)^k for every fixed r ≥ 3.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record for research mathematics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 194 issue 3 (2021)

events.direction: Partial progress toward the conjecture; consistent with it, but with a weaker base.

events.what_happened: Junichiro Fukuyama posts 'Improved Bound on Sets Including No Sunflower with Three Petals' (arXiv 1809.10318). It treats the three-petal case: a family of m-sets satisfying a Γ-condition with parameter c·m^(1/2+δ) contains three mutually disjoint sets, giving a 3-sunflower bound (c·m^(1/2+δ))^m. Per the arXiv comment on v3, v2 (January 2019) had a flaw in the induction step of the main proof; v3 (December 2021) fixes it and proves a slightly stronger claim. Predates the window.
events.revisions: v2 29 Jan 2019 (flawed induction step, per the v3 comment); v3 23 Dec 2021 (fix).
events.delivers: A restricted case: r = 3 petals only, with bound (c·m^(1/2+δ))^m for each δ in (0,1/2). The base c·m^(1/2+δ) grows with the set size m, so this is not of the form C^m and does not establish even the r = 3 case of the conjecture.
events.remains: The r = 3 case in the conjectured form C^m, and every r ≥ 4.
events.doubts: The author's own comment on v3 says v2 contained a flaw in the induction step; the v3 fix is not independently assessed in any source found.
events.direction: Restricted (r = 3) progress; consistent with the conjecture in direction, but the base is not of the conjectured form.

events.what_happened: Fukuyama posts 'The Sunflower Conjecture Proven' (arXiv 2212.13609), v1 on 27 December 2022. The v1 abstract reads: 'This paper proves the sunflower conjecture by confirming that a family F of sets each of cardinality at most m includes a k-sunflower, if |F| > [ck log (k+1)]^m for a constant c>0 independent of m and k.' The listing comment reads '10 pages. The paper is self-contained to verify.' Predates the window.
events.revisions: v2 27 Apr 2026, threshold changed to (ck)^(2m), comment '8 pages to fix the error of Ver. 1'. v3 22 Jun 2026, threshold changed to (ck^4)^m, comment '8 pages to fix the error of Ver. 2'. Current version is v3.
events.delivers: If correct, a full resolution in the conjectured shape: for every k, a family of sets of size at most m with more than [ck log(k+1)]^m members contains a k-sunflower, with c independent of m and k. The base depends on the petal count only, so as claimed it would cover every part of problem_asks. The abstract states no restriction. The author later says this version contained an error (see withdrawn).
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim held. The author's later comment means the claim is not established as stated in v1.
events.doubts: The author's own v2 comment says v1 contains an error. The threshold changed in each later version, and each change weakens the k-dependence: k log(k+1) in v1, k^2 in v2, k^4 in v3. Single author. No review, citation or forum discussion of v1 found in any source searched.

withdrawn.what: Author's comment on v2 says v1 contains an error, fixed by changing the bound from [ck log(k+1)]^m to (ck)^(2m)

events.direction: Claims a full proof of the conjecture (as the author's abstract states). The author has since said this version was wrong.

events.what_happened: Fukuyama posts 'Extensions of a Family for Sunflowers' (arXiv 2301.04219). The abstract studies the l-extension of families of m-sets and shows that under a Γ(8^(√log2 m)·√m·k·log2 k)-condition with m large relative to k, the family contains k mutually disjoint sets. It is a conditional result about a Γ-condition and does not claim the sunflower conjecture in the abstract. Predates the window.
events.delivers: A conditional statement about families satisfying a Γ-condition. It is a different hypothesis from the sunflower hypothesis as stated in problem_asks, so it settles no part of the problem.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Neither confirms nor refutes the conjecture; a conditional result on a different hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Anup Rao posts 'The Story of Sunflowers' (arXiv 2509.14790), a survey. The abstract says it 'discuss[es] recent progress towards the sunflower conjecture' and 'present[s] a short elementary proof of the best known bounds for the robust sunflower lemma'. It does not give a new bound for the general conjecture.
events.delivers: A survey and a new proof of existing robust-sunflower-lemma bounds. It establishes nothing new for the general conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Background; consistent with the conjecture still being open. The abstract itself does not say 'open'; a secondary summary of the survey does (not verified in the text read).

events.what_happened: Fukuyama posts 'Sunflower Bound with a Sub-Logarithmic Base' (arXiv 2510.19037). The abstract states: a family of sets each of size m > 2 with |F| ≥ (c k^2 ln m / ln ln m)^m includes a k-sunflower.
events.revisions: v2 1 Dec 2025, comment 'Minor errors in Ver. 1 fixed on 8 pages.'
events.delivers: A bound with base c k^2 ln m / ln ln m. The base grows with m, so it is not C(k)^m. It improves the known base but does not establish the conjectured exponential bound whose base depends on k only.
events.remains: The conjectured bound C(k)^m with the base independent of m, for every fixed petal count k.
events.doubts: The author's v2 comment says v1 had minor errors. Single author; no review found.
events.direction: Partial progress; consistent with the conjecture in direction, not of its form.

events.what_happened: Balogh, Bernshteyn, Delcourt, Ferber and Pham post 'Sunflowers in set systems with small VC-dimension' (arXiv 2408.04165). For ℓ-element families of VC-dimension at most d, more than (C r (log d + log* ℓ))^ℓ sets force an r-sunflower; when d = 1 the bound (r−1)^ℓ suffices and is described as sharp. The paper is published in Combinatorica 45(6), article 58, December 2025 (DOI 10.1007/s00493-025-00186-8).
events.revisions: v2 23 Sep 2025; journal version Combinatorica 45(6), December 2025.
events.delivers: Proves the sunflower statement only for families of bounded VC-dimension d. For d = 1 it gives the conjectured shape (r−1)^ℓ. For fixed d > 1 the base C r (log d + log* ℓ) depends on ℓ through log* ℓ, so it is not C(r)^ℓ even for bounded d. Does not claim the general conjecture.
events.remains: Families of unbounded VC-dimension, and for each fixed d > 1 the conjectured base independent of ℓ.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal of record for combinatorics
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, Combinatorica 45(6) article 58 (Dec 2025)

events.direction: Restricted-class progress consistent with the conjecture; the base is of the conjectured form only at d = 1.

events.what_happened: Kupavskii and Noskov post 'Linear dependencies, polynomial factors in the Duke–Erdős forbidden sunflower problem' (arXiv 2410.06156). The paper extends Frankl and Füredi's asymptotic solution of the Duke–Erdős problem to a wider range of parameters.
events.delivers: Results on the Duke–Erdős forbidden sunflower problem, a different extremal question (largest family with no s-sunflower of a given kernel size). It does not bear on the Erdős–Rado conjecture as stated.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Different problem; no bearing on the direction of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Ihringer and Kupavskii post 'The Erdős-Rado Sunflower Problem for Vector Spaces' (arXiv 2505.03671). It replaces sets with k-dimensional subspaces over a field with q elements, determines the largest s-sunflower-free family up to constant factors in the regimes considered, and uses lifted maximum rank-distance codes for the lower bounds.
events.delivers: An analogue of the problem for vector spaces, motivated by the set version. It is a different question and settles nothing about set families.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Analogue; no bearing on the direction of the set-family conjecture.

events.what_happened: Kupavskii and Noskov post 'Exact results and the structure of extremal families for the Duke–Erdős forbidden sunflower problem' (arXiv 2511.17142). It answers the Duke–Erdős question exactly for t = 2, odd s and k ≥ 5 with n large, and reduces the Duke–Erdős problem for large k and n to an Erdős–Rado-like problem depending on t and s only.
events.delivers: An exact answer for the Duke–Erdős problem in one range (t = 2, odd s, k ≥ 5, n large). That is a different problem. The reduction is to an Erdős–Rado-like problem, not a resolution of it.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Different problem; no bearing on the direction of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Quanyu Tang and Shengtong Zhang post 'Harmonic LCM patterns and sunflower-free capacity' (arXiv 2512.20055). The abstract gives an unconditional lower bound (log N)^(c_k − o(1)) for the harmonic-weighted LCM-k-free sum with fixed k ≥ 3, and relates it to the Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower capacity μ_k^S; it states the Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture fails for fixed k iff f_k(N) = (log N)^(1−o(1)).
events.delivers: A result on a related but different quantity (LCM-k-free harmonic weight and the Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower capacity for subsets of [N]). The abstract says the paper does not concern the full Erdős–Rado conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Related but different question; no bearing on the direction of the Erdős–Rado conjecture.

events.what_happened: Omran Ahmadi and Hassan Norouzi post 'A Polynomial Improvement of Naslund–Sawin Bound for Sunflower-Free Families Using Triangular Tensors' (arXiv 2606.30593). For sunflower-free families F ⊆ 2^[n] they claim |F| = O(n^(1/6) (3/2^(2/3))^n), improving the Naslund–Sawin bound's n^(1/2) factor.
events.delivers: A polynomial-factor improvement for the subsets-of-[n] version (Erdős–Szemerédi type). It is a different question: a bound on sunflower-free families in 2^[n], not the Erdős–Rado statement about k-uniform families for all k.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Different (subsets-of-[n]) question; no bearing on the direction of the Erdős–Rado conjecture.

events.what_happened: Tapas Kumar Mishra posts 'Erdős Rado Sunflower Theorem for Shifted Families' (arXiv 2606.02667; v2 8 June 2026). The abstract reads: 'In this paper, we prove the conjecture for shifted families.' The HTML's Theorem 1 (Section 6) gives f′(k,s) ≤ s^(2k) for k ≤ s−1 and f′(k,s) ≤ 2f′(k−1,s) otherwise, for shifted families.
events.delivers: The conjectured exponential shape, for shifted families only. The term 'shifted families' is not defined on the page read. Says nothing about general families.
events.remains: All families that are not shifted, i.e. the general conjecture.
events.doubts: The HTML's proof begins by assuming k ≥ s, which does not match the stated theorem's split at k ≤ s−1 (as read). The theorem's range is therefore not obviously the proof's range. A third-party review (Moonlight) describes the paper as proving the full conjecture, which the arXiv abstract does not claim (see disputes). The author has another claimed proof (Erdős matching conjecture) seen only in a search summary, not opened.
events.direction: Restricted-class proof consistent with the conjecture; the general case is not addressed.

events.what_happened: Fukuyama's v2 of 'The Sunflower Conjecture Proven' (arXiv 2212.13609), posted 27 April 2026. The abstract claims: a family of sets of size at most m with |F| > (ck)^(2m), c independent of m and k, includes a k-sunflower. The comment reads '8 pages to fix the error of Ver. 1.' The v2 body was not read.
events.delivers: If correct, the conjectured shape with base c^2 k^2, depending on the petal count only. No restriction stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Nothing, if correct; the author's later comment says v2 had an error.
events.doubts: The author's v3 comment says v2 contains an error ('8 pages to fix the error of Ver. 2'). The threshold changed from v1 and again in v3. Single author; no review found.

withdrawn.what: Author's comment on v3 says v2 contains an error, fixed by changing the threshold to (ck^4)^m

events.direction: Claims a full proof of the conjecture, as v1 did. The author has since said this version was wrong.

events.what_happened: Fukuyama's current version (v3, 22 June 2026) of 'The Sunflower Conjecture Proven' (arXiv 2212.13609). The abstract reads: 'We demonstrate the truth of the sunflower conjecture by showing that a family F of sets each of cardinality at most m includes a k-sunflower, if |F| > (ck^4)^m for a constant c>0 independent of m and k.' The comment reads '8 pages to fix the error of Ver. 2.' The HTML proof outline has: a pair-counting classification of pairs by intersection size (neighbour pairs); a counting lemma (Lemma 2.1); choice of a maximal core C (Lemma 2.2, Proposition 2.3); and greedy sunflower extraction (Algorithm S). The outline was read, not checked line by line.
events.revisions: v1 27 Dec 2022 (threshold [ck log(k+1)]^m); v2 27 Apr 2026 (threshold (ck)^(2m)); v3 22 Jun 2026 (threshold (ck^4)^m).
events.delivers: If correct, the conjectured shape with base c k^4, depending on the petal count only. No restriction stated. Taken at face value this resolves the problem as stated.
events.remains: Nothing, if correct. No source found assesses it.
events.doubts: Two earlier versions were self-described as erroneous, and the threshold changed in each. Single author; no preprint review, expert assessment, citation or forum discussion found across the Erdős forum thread for #20 (through 17 Sep 2026), Wikipedia, the 2025 Rao survey, or searches for reaction to Fukuyama's 2026 versions. The arXiv comments point to an external page for the proof, which was not located or read.
events.direction: Claims a full proof of the conjecture, in the conjecture's favour.

events.what_happened: A Zenodo preprint, 'A Proof of the Sunflower Conjecture' (record 18256089, v1, 15 January 2026), by Cody Mitchell (independent researcher), with 'Opus Claude, Anthropic' also listed as a co-creator. It claims a proof of the Sunflower Conjecture with an r-independent bound, supported by Theorem 1.2, Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 (the bound's numerical form is not on the page read; a search snippet gives (k−1)^(2r), not verified). The corrected record 18260198 ('On the Sunflower Conjecture: Computational Bounds and an Unsuccessful Proof Attempt', v2 correction notice, 15 January 2026) retracts the claim: 'Version 1 claimed a proof of the Sunflower Conjecture. This claim is RETRACTED.' It says 'Lemma 4.2 incorrectly bounds the piercing number independently of r, which is known to be impossible' and 'The Sunflower Conjecture remains OPEN.'
events.revisions: Record 18256089 (v1-retracted; page last modified 14 Jul 2026, marked RETRACTED); corrected record 18260198 (v2 correction notice, 15 Jan 2026). Concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18256088.
events.delivers: As claimed in v1: a proof of the conjecture with a bound independent of r. Retracted by the authors, so nothing in the retracted version is established. The corrected record states the conjecture remains open.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.

checked_by.qualification: Named mathematician. Search summaries describe him as maintaining erdosproblems.com; not confirmed on any page read.
checked_by.what_they_did: Identified the error in Lemma 4.2, per the authors' own correction notice. Not located in any independent source.

events.doubts: The error is stated by the authors: Lemma 4.2 bounds the piercing number independently of r, which the v2 notice calls known to be impossible. The Bloom critique rests on the authors' own statement; no public forum post or other source was found. The retracted v1 page says the error 'confused matching number with piercing number'.

withdrawn.what: Proof claim retracted by the authors: Theorem 1.2 (main result), Theorem 4.1 (universal piercing bound) and Lemma 4.2 all retracted

events.direction: Claimed a proof in the conjecture's favour; now retracted, so no direction is established.

systems.name: Opus Claude
systems.what_it_did: Not described anywhere in the record. It appears only as a co-creator entry ('Opus Claude, Anthropic' on v1; 'Claude, Opus' with Anthropic affiliation on v2). The sunflower-lean GitHub README lists the author line 'Cody Mitchell & Claude (Opus)'. Nothing states what the model did in the argument, so its role in the retracted proof is unknown.

events.what_happened: Forum user sproutseeds posts on the Erdős Problems forum, thread 20, on 26 February 2026. The post says the base cases f(1,3)=2 through f(6,3)=19 are formally certified in Lean 4, in the repository SproutSeeds/sunflower-lean, and that 'the general bound remains open'. It also reports weak-sunflower values M(n,3) for small n (M(1,3)=2 through M(4,3)=8 via Lean native_decide; n = 5 to 7 via a SAT solver with LRAT certificates). Terence Tao replied the same day that 'It appears that your Lean code is at least partially AI-generated (I see references to Aristotle, for instance)' and asked for AI-use disclosure under site policy. The post's edit reads: 'built collaboratively using intelligence systems, primarily OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.2, extra-high reasoning effort) via the Codex CLI, and Anthropic Claude (Opus 4.5 and 4.6) via the Claude CLI.'
events.revisions: Post edited to add the AI-tool sentence (date of edit not visible in the page read).
events.delivers: Finitely many values: f(n,3) for n ≤ 6, and weak-sunflower values M(n,3) for small n (a different problem, Erdős #857). The conjecture asserts a bound for all n, and finitely many instances do not move it under the scope rule. Nothing in the post addresses the universal bound.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the bound C(r)^k for every fixed r and all k.

machine_checked.sorry_free: Self-reported: the post and README say the proofs are sorry-free (README: the M3 results are 'all sorry-free'). Not verified; the repository was read but the build was not run.

events.directly_checkable: Small values can be re-derived by a finite search or SAT computation; the post cites LRAT certificates for the n = 5 to 7 weak-sunflower values.
events.doubts: M(1,3) to M(4,3) rely on Lean native_decide, which trusts compiled evaluation beyond the kernel. The Lean code is partly AI-generated, per Tao. The author's own README marks Spread.lean as 'Draft (not verified)'. The author cautions that some theorems may already be in the literature. The forum handle sproutseeds is linked to the repository, whose README author line is 'Cody Mitchell & Claude (Opus)'; that identity is an inference from the shared repository, not stated in any source.
events.direction: Finite base cases only; consistent with the conjecture, and does not decide the universal bound.
events.object: Lean-certified values f(n,3) for n = 1 to 6 (f(1,3)=2 through f(6,3)=19), and small weak-sunflower values M(n,3). No single extremal family is described in the post read.

events.what_happened: Forum user sammausberg posts a draft note of partial results on Erdős #20 in thread 20 (21 April 2026). The post says the note 'grew out of extensive AI-assisted exploration over many sessions, numbering in the hundreds', that the author has 'done my best to ensure that the Lean formalizations and proofs are correct', and that 'This is not a proof of the full exponential sunflower conjecture.' Per the thread summary read, its content is exact reductions and solved model classes, including F_{5,5}(2) = 16 and F_{4,4}(3) ≥ 28 (not f(n,3)), and the bound: if the trace family is itself k-sunflower-free, |G| ≤ f(r,k) f(m−r,k). The note itself was not located; this is from the forum post's summary as read.
events.delivers: Partial reductions and solved model classes, explicitly not the general bound. The specific values concern other parameters, not f(n,3).
events.remains: The general conjecture, and the bound for all n in f(n,3).

The only check beyond the author is an automated AI check, which the post links to a ChatGPT share, and it reports one minor issue. The note's own disclaimer limits it to partial results. The note appears nowhere outside the forum.

events.what_happened: Xuan Fang and Tianyu Wang post 'A Note on a Result of Chen Li' (arXiv 2609.18458, v1, 16 September 2026). The abstract says C. Li resolves the fractional version of Talagrand's discrete convexity problem, and that the note uses Li's method to answer another problem of Talagrand. The HTML's 'Statement of AI Usage' reads: 'The proof is developed by GPT6 under the authors' guidance, and is human-checked by the authors.' The HTML says the result answers Talagrand's Conjecture 7.8, and introduces the problem as 'closely linked to the sunflower problem posed by Erdős and Rado'.
events.delivers: Answers Talagrand's Conjecture 7.8 (spread measures stochastically dominated by product measures, up to averaging over subsets). That is a different problem. The sunflower link is only a remark in the introduction.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: The AI claim rests on the authors' own statement and is not verified. The PDF was unreadable here; the HTML was read.
events.direction: Different problem (Talagrand); no bearing on the direction of the Erdős–Rado conjecture.

systems.name: GPT6
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors, 'The proof is developed by GPT6 under the authors' guidance'. The result concerns Talagrand's problem, not the sunflower conjecture.

events.what_happened: Gennian Ge, Jian Wang, Zixiang Xu and Xiaochen Zhao post 'Bounded VC-dimension implies the Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture' (arXiv 2609.18995, v1, 17 July 2026; 9 pages). The abstract: for every fixed r ≥ 3 there is K(r) such that every ℓ-uniform family with more than K(r)^ℓ members contains an r-sunflower, and 'We prove this conjecture for families of bounded VC-dimension.' HTML Theorem 1.1: an ℓ-uniform family with VC(H) ≤ d and |H| > (50dr)^ℓ contains an r-sunflower.
events.revisions: v1 only, as of the read.
events.delivers: A linear-base bound (50dr)^ℓ for families of VC-dimension at most d. It removes the log* ℓ factor from Balogh et al. The base depends on d as well as r, so the result is exponential in ℓ for each fixed d. Restricted to bounded VC-dimension; it does not address families of unbounded VC-dimension.
events.remains: Families of unbounded VC-dimension, and any bound whose base depends on r alone for general families.
events.doubts: The abstract says 'this conjecture' but proves it only for bounded VC-dimension. The Erdős forum post by Alfaiz (17 September 2026) restates it as 'This conjecture has been proved for families of bounded VC-dimension', dropping the restriction (see disputes). Single source; no review found. The PDF was unreadable here; the HTML was read.
events.direction: Restricted-class proof of the conjectured exponential shape, with base depending on d and r.

events.what_happened: Edward Axante, Cristian Budala, David Chitic, Bogdan Dumitru and Mihai Nacu post 'Sunflower-Free Uniform Families: Recursive Constructions and Explicit Bounds' (arXiv 2609.06175, v1, 5 September 2026). The abstract: a recursive construction gives a general lower bound on the exponential growth rate of f(w,k); a general upper bound is proved for 3-uniform families with at least four petals; explicit bounds 39 ≤ f(3,4) ≤ 49, f(3,5) ≤ 146, 153 ≤ f(3,6) ≤ 255, 259 ≤ f(3,7) ≤ 474, 54 ≤ f(4,3) ≤ 83, and an intersecting 4-uniform family with no 3-petal sunflower has maximum size 27. 'The upper bounds 49 and 83 are computer-assisted.' Introduction, Theorem 3.5: the growth base B(k) = lim f(w,k)^(1/w) satisfies B(k) ≥ r_k, with r_k = (k + √(k²−2k))/2 for even k.
events.delivers: A lower bound on the exponential base of f(w,k), of order k, consistent with the conjecture's exponential shape. It does not bound the upper growth. Finite values for small w and k bear on finitely many instances, which by the scope rule do not move a universal claim. The general upper bound stated in the abstract, for 3-uniform families with at least four petals, is a restricted case whose form was not read.
events.remains: The general upper bound C(r)^w for all w and all r ≥ 3.
events.directly_checkable: The explicit finite constructions (for example 39 ≤ f(3,4)) can be checked by a finite computation; the method for the 'computer-assisted' upper bounds is not described in the text read.
events.doubts: Single preprint. The 3-uniform upper bound and the method behind the computer-assisted bounds were not read. A search snippet claimed an AI-assisted workflow in the acknowledgements; the HTML version has no acknowledgements and no such statement, so the snippet is not supported.
events.direction: Lower-bound progress on the base; does not address the upper bound that the conjecture asserts.
events.object: Explicit families for the finite lower bounds (for example 39 ≤ f(3,4) and 54 ≤ f(4,3)) and a recursive construction giving the exponential lower bound with base r_k. The constructions are explicit, not existential.

disputes.summary: The Erdős forum post by Alfaiz (17 Sep 2026) says 'This conjecture has been proved for families of bounded VC-dimension', citing the Ge et al. preprint. The arXiv abstract restricts the claim to bounded VC-dimension. A Moonlight literature review describes Mishra's shifted-families preprint as claiming the full conjecture; the arXiv abstract claims only shifted families. Both overstate the arXiv abstracts.

Fukuyama's preprint has three arXiv versions (2022, April 2026, June 2026). The author's comments say v1 and v2 each contained an error, and the stated threshold changes each time: [ck log(k+1)]^m, then (ck)^(2m), then (ck^4)^m. The current version is not endorsed by any source found.

The Zenodo records list 'Opus Claude, Anthropic' (and 'Claude, Opus' with Anthropic affiliation) as co-creators. No statement from Anthropic, and no sentence from the authors describing what the model did, was found. The affiliation is unverified.

summary: Searched 35 times, opened 39 sources (arXiv abstracts and HTML, journal and repository records, the Erdős Problems problem page, thread, history and two user profiles, Wikipedia, Kalai's project page, the Polymath blog, Quanta, and two GitHub repositories); PDFs for four preprints were unreadable and the HTML was used instead. As of 13 October 2026 the problem is listed open on erdosproblems.com (no status change; history's latest entry 7 March 2026) and no source found states that it is settled. The only refereed in-window result is Balogh et al. (Combinatorica, December 2025), restricted to bounded VC-dimension and of the conjectured exponential shape only at d = 1. Ge et al. (July 2026) extend this to a linear base for bounded VC-dimension, and Mishra (June 2026) claims the conjecture for shifted families; neither has been checked by anyone found. Fukuyama's 'The Sunflower Conjecture Proven' is the one in-window claim of the full statement that still stands on arXiv. It was first posted in December 2022 with a threshold [ck log(k+1)]^m and has been revised twice (April and June 2026) with the author stating each earlier version contained an error; no engagement with any version was found. A Zenodo proof by Cody Mitchell with 'Opus Claude, Anthropic' listed as co-creator (January 2026) is retracted by its authors, who say Lemma 4.2 is wrong and attribute the error to Thomas Bloom; that attribution rests on the authors' own notice. The AI-involved work on the Erdős forum is partial: sproutseeds's Lean certification of f(n,3) for n ≤ 6 (26 Feb 2026) credits OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.2), Anthropic Claude (Opus 4.5 and 4.6) and Aristotle, and Tao called the Lean code at least partly AI-generated; sammausberg's partial note (21 Apr 2026) credits unnamed 'AI-assisted exploration', and its only check is an automated AI check. Harjas Sandhu's forum post of 18 July 2026 reports failed attempts with ChatGPT 5.5 Pro, codex and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, and so is recorded as a dead end, not an event. The 'AI+ Math polymath project' that Kalai linked on 17 July 2026 is a project page with no AI content; the Polymath 'AI' post of 3 April 2026 does not mention sunflowers. The Chen Li note (Fang and Wang, Sept 2026) credits 'GPT6' with a proof, but on Talagrand's problem, not the sunflower conjecture. Where a call was close: the Fukuyama v3 claim is the only full-statement claim that might count as resolving the problem, and whether it does rests on a proof I read in outline but did not verify, by an author who has twice said his previous version was wrong. Its base has the conjectured shape (depending on k only), and I have recorded it as a claim, not a result. Also close: whether Ge et al. or Mishra count as partial resolutions is for the judging pass; I recorded the restriction in each record. Per the scope rule, the finite values f(n,3) for n ≤ 6 and the small-case bounds in Axante et al. do not move the universal claim. Context recorded in events and summary: the Wikipedia article states that the best general bound is C = O(r log k) (Bell, Chueluecha and Warnke, 2021), which I did not open. Also context: Alon, Shpilka and Umans (2011/2012) show that the conjecture, if true, would rule out certain matrix multiplication approaches; a Dogmachine forum post of 30 April 2026 cites this, and it is not a 2026 event.
competing_reading: Read Fukuyama's v3 (22 June 2026, threshold (ck^4)^m) as a full resolution. It has the conjectured shape, it is the only full-statement claim still standing on arXiv, and it has been public for almost four months with no reported error. On that reading the problem moved in June 2026, and the author's earlier errors are routine for a self-proof. The opposite reading, which the record supports, is that the claim has been revised twice with the author conceding error each time, has no review or engagement in the sources found, and the threshold weakened with each revision. Under that reading the problem is open and the only in-window human-checked results are restricted-class. A third reading treats Ge et al. and Mishra as partial resolutions, which the restrictions in the abstracts do not support as a settlement of the general statement.
what_would_settle_it: For Fukuyama v3: a referee report, an erratum, a sorry-free Lean formalisation, or a written assessment from a combinatorialist on the Erdős forum or a blog (the pair-counting outline and Lemma 2.1 are the points to check). For Ge et al. and Mishra: a statement whether K depends on VC-dimension (Ge et al.) or what 'shifted families' means in Mishra (the term is not defined in the text read). For the AI items: the full text of sammausberg's note and sproutseeds's sunflower-lean repository build with the native_decide lemmas re-checked by the kernel; an authors' sentence saying what the model contributed to the Mitchell proof; and the public forum or Lemma 4.2 correspondence Thomas Bloom is said to have made. For the Erdős site status: a change in the erdosproblems.com entry for #20.

(2) The full text of Rao's survey, ALWZ, Fukuyama 1809.10318, Fukuyama 2510.19037, Kupavskii–Noskov (both), Ihringer–Kupavskii, Tang–Zhang and Ahmadi–Norouzi was not read; only abstracts and listing pages. (6) The sunflower-lean repository was read but not built; its 'sorry-free' status is self-reported. (7) Forum thread 20 had four hidden comments not read.
